sample_unit: patient information sheets (7 procedures x 2 models)

links.outcome: Currency of ChatGPT-generated nuclear medicine patient information rated by expert assessors
links.effect: GPT-3.5 lacked accuracy and currency and omitted important information; GPT-4 was enhanced across appropriateness, accuracy, and currency despite some omissions.
links.quote: ChatGPT powered by GPT-3.5 provided patient information that was appropriate in terms of being patient-facing but lacked accuracy and currency and omitted important information.

links.outcome: Accuracy and omissions in ungrounded LLM-generated patient information sheets rated by expert assessors
links.effect: GPT-3.5 sheets were inaccurate and not fit for purpose; GPT-4 improved accuracy but still omitted some information and was largely fit for purpose.
links.quote: GPT-4 provided patient information enhanced across appropriateness, accuracy, and currency, despite some omission of information.

screen.reason: The study empirically evaluates and compares the accuracy and fitness of patient information sheets generated by GPT-3.5 vs GPT-4 for nuclear medicine procedures using expert assessment, but does not test a specific deployment guardrail or practice.
